newsitem.title: UK: G20 in talks with ECHO, Multinet over FX venture.
newsitem.headline: G20 in talks with ECHO, Multinet over FX venture.

text.p: The Group of 20 (G20) banks said in a statement on Thursday it was in talks with Exchange Clearing House (ECHOE) and Multinet International Bank (Multinet) over forming an integrated foreign exchange settlement venture.

The three groups "confirmed that they are in discussions with a view towards forming an integrated industry owned venture for the reduction of settlement and pre-settlement risk in the foreign exchange market".

The statement added: "These discussions, which are expected to conclude soon, include opportunities for cooperation on the development of the continuous linked settlement system, broadening the ownership and usage of the system, and increasing participation in multilateral netting."
The G20 said in its statement it was establishing a British-based company called CLS Services to begin development work on its plans for a foreign exchange settlement system.

"At its recent meeting in London, the Group of 20 banks confirmed its commitment to develop and implement a continuous linked settlement system to reduce significantly foreign exchange settlement risk," the group said.
"The G20 expressed this commitment with a decision to form CLS Services Ltd, a private UK company to be incorporated in July 1997 for the purpose of commencing development work," it said.
The group said its members were expected to become shareholders of the company.
Continuous Linked Settlements is effectively a method whereby deals are concluded when payments on both sides are simultaneously made.
The G20, formed in 1994, comprises the following banks:

ABN AMRO, Bank of America, Bankers Trust, Barclays Bank, Banque Nationale de Paris, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi, Chase, CIBC, Citibank, Credit Suisse, Deutsche Bank, Dresdner Bank, Fuji Bank, HSBC Holdings, J.P. Morgan, National Westminster, Royal Bank of Canada, Swiss Bank Corp, Societe Generale and UBS.
The G20 statement did not specify financial details about the new company or investments by G20 members.
